Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Jane Austen (author, Wikidata Q36322), died 1877; Austin Dobson (notes, Wikidata Q3595615), died 1921; Hugh Thomson (illustrator, Wikidata Q3142319), died 1920. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Austen, Jane, 1775-1817; Dobson, Austin, 1840-1921 [Commentator]; Thomson, Hugh, 1860-1920 [Illustrator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: Jane Austen [1817, 1877]).

Printed edition: Sense and Sensibility, Pantheon Books, 1811, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/sensesensibility0000jane_j9p4. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 88%, 90%, 94% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Austin Dobson, Hugh Thomson, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
